# One WINDOW Linux comparison

This is the diagnostic authorized by approval `7b5f1b26-94ad-470a-b912-ba7e9b08a97d`. It cannot satisfy required CI or integration acceptance. The workflow commit selects two separately committed application descendants in `sources.json`; it is not either tested application source. Both descendants contain exactly the six-line `success-retention.patch`, SHA256 `4e34f31f0028c7ba9ad495259f60046a25232e5b59019ce94c6a7b1e207cfb58`. Their foundations, parents, trees, source delta and identical unchanged lockfile are checked before setup.

The existing registered `ci.yml` path becomes manual-only on the isolated diagnostic ref. It allocates one standard Ubuntu 24.04 job for at most 120 minutes, with no retry, matrix or follow-up dispatch. It prepares both source environments before a strict build or substantive runtime. C executes before T; at most two strict builds and two original Stable runtime invocations occur. The actual owner retains its original scene, two cases, three reloads, 42-second admission and 10-second evaluation limits, browser arguments, source/auth validators, one worker and zero test retries. The two package prereqs run unchanged before the external caller invokes the exported owner with only observer hooks.

Environment preflight requires the approved image, OS, actual ancestor Runner.Worker version, Node and browser version. It records CPU count/model hash, memory, browser executable hash bound to the actual owned headless-shell child, and blank-page graphics backend/hash. This blank-page preflight is not a product runtime invocation. An unavailable or mismatched environment stops without fallback. Serial order, dependency installation, browser warmup and cache/workload variance limit causal inference.

Each source has a fresh clone/dependency installation, synthetic auth session and private output roots. The prerequisite migration database has a narrow acknowledged creation/OID owner tied to the existing Docker service inspector and actual SQL network. It does not inspect or remove the Stable owner's database or role. The original Stable owner creates and cleans its separate least-privilege role/database using unchanged transport attestation. No removed-attestation bypass, session termination, forced drop, profiler or lifecycle substitution is used. Original owner and child failures remain separate from observer errors; T requires actual retained terminal absence, zero sessions, removed root, no canonical cleanup issues, no observer errors, and successful prerequisite DB cleanup/connection close.

All inherited command streams and raw report/context/receipt files stay private on the runner. The adapter copies synchronously before canonical deletion, catches its own errors and constructs fresh fixed-field projections. Raw DOM, attachments, arbitrary errors, auth records, environment maps and transport files are never selected for upload. Unknown fields/names, unavailable documents and cap failures are counted; metadata-only error context explicitly omits content. Source lifecycle validation and physical byte descriptors bind cleanup projection before root removal. Success also matches the owner's final receipt. Stream observation includes independent browser clocks and host receipt timing; its capture/projection overhead is recorded and is not assumed zero.

The PostgreSQL service reads its synthetic password from the runner/container's privately compared boot-ID file. This is host-visible metadata, not a secret from other runner processes. No password value is present in YAML or command arguments. Docker logging is disabled for this ephemeral service so PostgreSQL query errors cannot disclose role passwords through automatic teardown logs. Service health, image, network identity and cleanup receipts remain observed; raw server logs are unavailable. The official PostgreSQL entrypoint supports the file input: https://github.com/docker-library/postgres/blob/master/15/bookworm/docker-entrypoint.sh .

One upload is limited to 100 MiB including its checksum inventory and seven days retention. Immediately before upload, the verifier checks the exact sealed inventory, regular-file containment, physical hashes and total bytes again. Failure or timeout without a safe seal produces no fallback raw upload. A failed C command remains failed even if T passes; neither passing result rehabilitates earlier CI5.

Focused local validation uses Node unit fixtures and lexical extraction of the actual C/T success owner for callback ordering. Fixture lifecycle data is not execution evidence; no local build, database or browser is run by these tests. In the task-owned layout (sibling `c-source` and `t-source` checkouts with their own dependencies), run `node --test .github/diagnostics/window-linux/focused.test.mjs`. The repository's pinned actionlint owner checks the workflow. Remote execution is performed only once after independent review and external publication checks. Deleting the isolated diagnostic ref later would remove its route; no production source rollback is needed.
